definitions.gloss: disliking something without trying it; prejudice without experience
definitions.explanation: originally refers to disliking food without tasting it, but commonly used to describe any prejudice against something one hasn't actually experienced

examples.japanese: ピーマンは{食|く}わず{嫌|ぎら}いだった。
examples.english: I disliked bell peppers without ever trying them.

examples.japanese: {食|く}わず{嫌|ぎら}いしないで、{一度|いちど}{試|ため}してみて。
examples.english: Don't dismiss it without trying - give it a shot.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{食|く}わず{嫌|ぎら}いしてはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't dismiss new technology without trying it.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Literally means "disliking without eating" ({食|く}わず = without eating, {嫌|ぎら}い = dislike).

USAGE:
- {食|く}わず{嫌|ぎら}いする (to dislike without trying)
- {食|く}わず{嫌|ぎら}いをやめる (to stop judging without trying)

BROADER MEANING:
While originally about food, this expression is commonly applied to any situation where someone has prejudice against something they haven't experienced - movies, music, activities, places, etc.

OPPOSITE CONCEPT:
Trying something before judging: {まずは{食|た}べてみる} (try eating it first)
